instructions:
Drives the running DJApp (dj-vevr-se) on this Mac: two decks, A and B, each playing a sample or a live Petri-net track. Call dj_state first. Everything sent here goes through the same path as the app's own buttons, so it is recorded when a session is recording. Audio plays on the Mac's speakers — you cannot hear it; read dj_state instead.

You can compose, not just select: dj_compose takes a piano roll you write (parts, notes, tempo) and plays exactly those notes on a deck as a Petri-net track — a specific song, not a generator seed. Reach for it when asked for a particular melody, riff, chord progression or arrangement; use dj_generate / dj_load_share to explore the generator's own space.

Words matter. "Inspired by <artist>" (or "<artist>-style") → dj_inspired: an original piece that reads the artist's general style (tempo, key, progression, groove, sound palette, form), never their melody, hook or lyric. "Import / play this file" → dj_import (a .mid today, MusicXML next; only material the user owns or that is public domain / Creative Commons, whose licence the share records). A request to transcribe or reproduce a specific copyrighted song's melody is declined: offer an inspired original instead.

tools.name: dj_state
tools.description: Snapshot of the app: per deck (title, mode sample|net, playing, bpm, position, sections and the current one, roles and which are on, volume/filter/pitch, quantize, next track, fixes {pass: whether dj's musicality pass rewrote the net — false for a raw-nets share, which plays the runner-only fixes —, names: the fixes it plays with}, level: the deck's short-term / momentary LUFS, autoGain on/off and the autoGainDB a sample plays at, the sample's own LUFS when levelled, a net deck's limiter), crossfader, master, the LOOP-record clips, the ones removed from the row and the loop channel (loops; loops.follow: the Tempo mode and the deck followed), connected controllers, recording, status line, locked (buttons disabled by right-click, by lock key), headphones (mix, level, pfl per deck), inpulseOutput (the Inpulse's audio device and whether it is routed, or null), awake (screen kept awake), view (which panels are open), scope (open, kind, source, measured), stage (window open and its toolbar settings), crates, saved voice variations by instrument, autoMix (the two-deck autopilot: on, bars, every, phase off|idle|playing|paused|preparing|armed|mixing, playing / incoming deck, handoffs, handoffBar and handoffInBars, next {genre, seed, cid, kind seed|instrument|genre|cued, move}, fader auto|user, paused / resumesInBars, idle: why it can't act, log of hand-offs newest first), and the app's build (id, version, build = git commit, date).

tools.name: dj_perform
tools.description:
Apply one deck action, as a button or fader in the app would. `action` is an object with `op` plus fields:
play {deck, on} · cue {deck} · hotCue/clearCue {deck, slot 0-7} · loop {deck, loop: in|out|halve|double} · param {deck, name: volume|filter|gain|eqLow|eqMid|eqHigh|pitch|reverbWet|reverbSize|reverbTone|autoGain, value} (0…1, 0.5 = centre for filter/gain/eq; autoGain 0/1 = sample loads levelled to the app's loudness; pitch is -1…1 = ±8%, 0 = none; reverb: wet 0 = off, size 0…1 = 0.25…8 s decay, tone 0 dark … 1 bright) · crossfader {value 0…1, 0 = A} · master {value} · nextTrack {deck} · autoAdvance {deck, on} · section {deck, index} · role {deck, role, on} · roleDisable {deck, role, on}: on = the role stays off through new tracks too, until disabled again with on false · macro {deck, macro: id from dj_catalog, a net macro or a master-chain FX / pitch / feel one; a sample deck takes the master-chain ones (vinyl-brake too), on its next bar} · panic {deck} · stinger {deck, n 0-3}: Hit n+1, curated from the genre and palette (a one-shot, a macro or a loop on the loop row; dj_state.decks.X.stingers says which) · sync {deck, align: beat|bar|tempo} · quantize {deck, mode: off|beat|bar} · follow {deck, leader: deck or null} · grid {deck, bpm > 0, offset s}: a sample deck's beat grid by hand (the first beat at offset seconds into the sample), replacing the analysis · queueNext {deck, share: {genre, seed, structure?}} · wander {deck, on} (works on dj_compose / dj_import tracks too, on the moves that need no seed: mutes, STEMS, macros, FX, stingers, palette hops, and layer moves: a library vocal / riser / texture loop comes in over the track, is swapped for another of its kind, or goes out): the deck walks by itself, one move per phrase (a mute, a macro, a stinger, the next seed, another instrument, structure or genre, swapped in at the next bar), drawn from its configuration so a recording replays the same walk; dj_state.decks.X.wander shows on, pace, nextMoveInBars, paused (the browser wheel steers and pauses it for a phrase), locks and the log of moves · wanderPace {deck, bars: 4|8|16|32} · wanderLock {deck, dimension: genre|tempo|key|structure|instruments|arrangement|fx|palette|layers|keep:<role>, on}: what the walk must not change (tempo: within 6 % of now; palette: the deck's sound palette; layers: no loop comes in, swaps or goes out; keep:bass keeps the bass's instrument and never mutes it) · loopRecord {deck, on, bars?}: LOOP record, held (on true) then let go (on false): the deck's bars from the downbeat before the press to the one after the release become a clip, looping under the mixer (dj_state.loops); with bars (1-64) on the press, a release within 250 ms records exactly that many bars from that downbeat instead (the app's tap length is dj_state.loops.tapBars) · grabBars {deck, bars}: the last bars whole bars the deck already played (up to ~21 s back), ending on the downbeat just gone, become a clip looping at once · clipLoop {id, on}: a clip in or out under the mixer on the next launch boundary (several loop at once; dj_state.loops.clips[].switchIn is the beats until a waiting one switches) · clipGain {id, value 0…1} · loopQuantize {beats: 1|4|8|16|32}: what loops launch on (a beat, a bar, 2/4/8 bars of the reference deck, phrases on its bars 1, 5, 9…; default 4) · loopFollow {mode: louder|source}: which deck the loops' tempo follows (louder: the louder playing deck, the default; source: each loop the deck it was taken from) · sceneSave {name}: the loops playing now (and their levels and FX) as a scene (overwrites one of that name) · sceneLaunch {name}: its loops in, every other out, all on the next launch boundary · sceneRename {name, to} · sceneDelete {name} (dj_state.loops.scenes, .quantize) · clipCrop {id, from, to}: keep its beats from..<to · clipRetune {id, voices: {"<MIDI channel>": instrument}}: a loop taken from a net rendered again with those instruments (the others as taken; channels as dj_state's voices number them), taking its place as a crop does, in phase if it is looping; refused for samples, sequences and takes with macros running · clipSequence {steps: [{clip, repeats}], replacing?}: join clips into a sequence (or rewrite one) · clip {deck: L|A|B, id}: move a clip onto a deck (L = under the mixer) · clipRemove {id}: off the row, its audio kept (dj_state.loops.removed; dj_loops undo puts it back, and has the row's load source, export and stop all) · clipRestore {id, at?}: a removed clip back where it was (or at index at) · clipForget {id}: delete a removed clip for good · clipRename {id, title} · clipColor {id, color: red|orange|yellow|green|teal|blue|violet|pink or null} · clipMute {id, on}: silent but still looping, in phase · clipSolo {id, on}: while any clip is soloed only soloed ones are heard · clipKeyLock {id, on}: at another tempo it keeps its pitch (a time-stretched copy, made in the background; dj_state.loops.clips[].stretched) · clipFx {id, fx: {drive 0…24 dB, mode clean|soft|hard|tube|fold|crush, amount 0…1, bits 1…16, downsample 1…32, tone 0…1 (1 open), mix 0…1, trim −24…12 dB, autoLevel, bypass}}: after effects on a loop under the mixer, on top of its dry audio (missing fields default; {} is off; dj_state.loops.clips[].fx) · clipImport {id, title, bpm, beats, provenance?}: outside audio already in the sample library (by content id) onto the row as a clip, looping from the next launch boundary; the same audio twice is one clip (dj_stock_loops addToRow is the way in for a stock loop; a set with one is never published) · loopKeyLock {on}: the row's key lock, for clips without their own · loopFade {fade: off|10ms|beat|bar}: how loops come in and go out (default 10ms) · clipQuantize {id, beats: 1|4|8|16|32 or null}: one loop's own launch boundary (null: the row's loopQuantize; a scene switches on the row's) · clipFade {id, fade: off|10ms|beat|bar or null}: one loop's own fade (null: the row's loopFade) · clipFollow {id, mode: louder|source or null}: whose tempo one loop follows (null: the row's loopFollow) · tapBars {bars: 1-64 or null}: what a quick tap of a controller's LOOP records (dj_state.loops.tapBars is the app's) · voiceTweak {deck, channel, params}: shape a net deck's channel's synth voice live, on the song playing (no reload; channel from dj_state.voices[].channel): params {gainDB -48…24, attack s, decayScale × note length, maxDecay s, lowpass Hz (0 = off), distortion 0…1, vibratoRate Hz, vibratoDepth 0…0.1 of the frequency, pitchFrom / pitchTo × the note, pitchTime s (0 = no sweep)}, each optional (unset = the instrument's own); {} resets to the instrument's voice. Session-only: it lasts for the song on that deck (its section jumps and other instrument picks), not a new track, a favorite or a relaunch; dj_state.voices[].tweak shows it · voiceSynth {deck, channel, on}: a sampled channel (dj_state.voices[].sampled) plays its synth voice (on) or its sample · clipMove {id, before: id or null}: move a clip on the row to just before another (null: the end) · lock {key, on}: lock an action like right-click ▸ Disable (key e.g. "A.play"; locked controller bindings do nothing) · setPalette {deck, palette: id from dj_palettes or null = the default}: the track's whole sound from a palette, at the next bar, kept for every new track on the deck · setRoleVoice {deck, role: kit|bass|melody|harmony|arp|stinger, voice: an option from dj_palettes / dj_state.decks.X.sound[].options (gm:4, synth:pwm-lead, cat:keys.epiano, inst:piano, a kit id…) or null = back to the palette}: one role's sound, kept through new tracks until reset · setKit {deck, kit: a kit id or null} · mixOut {deck, bars? 1-64, default 16}: play the deck out: at the next bar it jumps to the song's outro (or, in it or with none, plays on where it is), plays only its drums and bass for bars bars and stops on a bar line (the room rings out; section jumps keep it, a new track drops it) · mixIn {deck, bars? 1-64, default 4}: bring the deck in drums-forward: from the next bar its melodic parts rest for bars bars and come back on the bar line after · rewind {deck}: back to the start (a sample's first frame, a net's tick 0) · focus {deck: A|B|L}: aim the deck-less controls (keys, joystick, seed, wander) as a controller's deck-select does (dj_state.focus) · stemMute {deck, stem: music|mic, on}: a net deck's STEMS group muted or back (music: all but the drums; mic: the lead) · masterFx {deck, key: hp-freq|lp-freq|phaser-freq|phaser-depth|phaser-wet|crush-bits|distortion|master-pitch, value 0…1}: move a master FX slider by hand, value the fraction of its travel (as a controller fader sends it; master-pitch −12…12 semitones, the rest 0…100), on a net's chain, a sample deck's bus or the loops' (L) · fx {deck, param: filter|hp|lp|phaser-mix|phaser-depth|phaser-rate|crush|drive|pitch|room|echo|feedback, value}: the FX unit, live on the deck's chain (A, B or L): smoothed over ~30 ms, not quantised; value in the param's travel (filter −1…1: left LP, right HP, 0 off; pitch −12…12 semitones; the rest 0…1; neutral: lp 1, phaser-depth 0.5, the rest 0); room / echo / feedback are a net deck's sends (its genre's room and echo: 0 = as composed, 1 = 4× the send / feedback 0.92), not on sample decks or L; master macros ride on top of the unit and release back to it · fxReset {deck, onBeat?}: every FX unit control to neutral and its kill off (onBeat: on the deck's next beat) · fxKill {deck, on, onBeat?}: bypass the FX unit keeping its knobs, or back (dj_state.fxUnit) · autoMix {on, bars: 4|8|16|32 (default 8), every: 0|4|8|16 (default 0)}: the two-deck autopilot, the whole setting at once: while one deck plays, a phrase before the hand-off the other gets a neighbouring track (the next seed, another instrument, or a neighbouring genre the pitch fader reaches; a compatible key; both decks' wander locks hold; a net you load on the idle deck yourself is used as-is), starts on a phrase boundary synced, comes in drums-forward while the playing deck mixes out over bars bars, the crossfader stepping across bar by bar; every 0 = a song to its outro (a loop 8 phrases), else that many 8-bar phrases; steering pokes (play, cue, loops, sync, sections, loads, the seed wheel, the jog) pause it for a phrase, knobs / mutes / macros / FX don't; dj_state.autoMix · autoMixNow {}: hand off at the next phrase boundary at least 4 bars away · autoMixDefer {handoff}: recorded by the app itself when a compose is late; refused here. Deck "L" also takes param volume / mute (1 = muted), and macro (master-chain ids only: the loops' master FX, on the next loop bar) and panic; loopFxLink {on}: a master macro on deck A / B fires on the loops too (dj_state.loops.masterFx).
Net-only ops (section, role, net macros, stinger, mixOut, mixIn) need a deck in net mode; master-chain macros and panic also work on a sample deck (dj_state's macrosRunning). Use dj_generate, not op load, to put a new track on a deck.

tools.name: dj_generate
tools.description: Compose a live Petri-net track and load it on a deck (takes a few seconds; returns when loaded). Does not start playback — follow with dj_perform play.

options.description: Opt-in composition techniques (all off by default; part of the track's share/CID): hook (bool: one 1–2 bar chord-tone hook in every melody section) · hookBars (1|2) · chordSnap (off|strong|all: melody notes on beats 1+3 / every beat moved to the sounding chord) · chordSnapArp (bool: snap the arp too) · layerBudget ("auto" or 1–8: max melodic roles per section, bass > melody > harmony > arp) · bassFollow (bool: one bass pattern on the chord plan) · keyLock (bool: tension phrases stay in key) · melodyDensity, bassDensity (0–1] · ghostNotes, syncopation (0–1) · humanize (0–100). The same keys are also accepted at the top level.

palette.description: A sound palette id from dj_palettes; omit to keep the deck's (it carries to new tracks)

seed.description: Any number; same genre + seed = same track

structure.description: minimal | standard | extended for a song with sections; omit for an endless loop

tools.name: dj_catalog
tools.description: Genres, song structures, macro ids and deck names the other tools accept.

tools.name: dj_palettes
tools.description: The sound palettes a track can play from (Studio = each instrument's own sound, Synth, Synthwave, 8-bit, Acoustic band, Orchestral, Lo-fi tape, Jazz club, Club, Ambient, …): id, label, description, whether it plays on this Mac (`unavailable` says why not), local-only ones (never published), Wander's neighbours and each role's options. With `deck`, also what each of that deck's roles plays (`sound`). Set one with dj_perform setPalette, one role with setRoleVoice.

tools.name: dj_load_file
tools.description: Load an audio file from this Mac onto a deck as a sample.

tools.name: dj_load_share
tools.description: Load a beats (beats.bitwrap.io) share onto a deck as a live Petri-net track, exactly as the share describes it: a composed share (genre + seed + traits, overrides, overlays) is composed here; a raw-nets share plays its nets as given (arranged if it has a structure; to write your own notes use dj_compose). Takes a few seconds; returns the deck when loaded, with `share` = {kind net|rawNets, cid}. Does not start playback — follow with dj_perform play. A short ?cid= link without &z= can't be loaded (its payload is on a server): pass the full link or the payload.

link.description: A full share URL (https://beats.bitwrap.io/?cid=…&z=…, or just its ?query; the CID is verified), a legacy ?p= / ?g= link, or the envelope payload as JSON text (e.g. {"genre":"techno","seed":42})

tools.name: dj_compose
tools.description: Write a song and play it: a piano roll you compose becomes a live Petri-net track on a deck, playing exactly your notes (no generator, no musicality pass). Each part is a step-sequencer net of sixteenth-note steps (16 steps = one 4/4 bar, step 0 = bar 1 beat 1; 4 steps = a beat), looping; all parts share one length so they stay in phase. Parts are keyed by role: kick, snare, hihat, clap (drums; `note` may be left out: GM 36 / 38 / 42 / 39), bass, melody, harmony, arp. Each takes {instrument?, channel?, notes}; a note is [step, midi, dur?, vel?] (dur in sixteenths, default 2 for tonal parts and 1 for drums; vel 1–127, default 100; middle C = 60). Notes on the same step (chords) are fine: they play together. `steps` defaults to the roll's length rounded up to whole bars (max 1024). A part repeats a pattern with {every, from?, until?, notes}: the notes (steps relative to the pattern) recur every `every` steps from step `from` up to `until` (default `steps`, which a repeat needs if no `until`), so a bar of drums is written once; give a LIST of such segments for an arrangement (a part enters at bar 5 with from 64). Without `every` notes sit at `from` + step. Write the whole form out (8–64 bars) with a clear key and chord plan, not one riff. `layers` bring library vocals / risers / impacts in over it as parallel loops (see the argument); they follow the deck's tempo. Takes a few seconds, returns the deck with share {kind rawNets, cid} and `saved`, the file it was kept in (dj_compositions lists and reloads them). Does not start playback — follow with dj_perform play. Roles light up in dj_state like any net deck, so dj_perform (role mutes, macros, FX) and the controllers work on it. A deck that is playing keeps playing on load.

deck.description: A or B (not needed with load false)

energy.description: How hard it hits, 0–1 (kept for set planning)

key.description: Its key, e.g. "A minor" (kept for set planning)

tuple: Library sounds (vocals, risers, impacts, textures) that come in over the track as parallel tracks on the loop channel: [{loop: name|path, bar: N or [N,…] (the 1-based bar it comes in on), bars?: how long it stays (default one pass of the loop), gain?: dB under unity −24…0 (default −3), keyLock?: keep its pitch at another tempo (default true)}]. Find loops with dj_stock_loops list (category Vocals, Sound Effect, Texture/Atmosphere; near=<the track's bpm>). Launched a bar early so the loop bank's quantizing lands them on the bar; the track is local only, never published.

load.description: false = stage it: save the track (and add it to `set`) without loading a deck, so a whole set can be pre-rolled

tuple: {role: {instrument?: string, channel?: 1-16, every?, from?, until?, notes: [[step, midi, dur?, vel?], …]}} or a list of such segments, e.g. {"kick":{"every":16,"until":256,"notes":[[0],[4],[8],[12]]},"bass":{"instrument":"sub-bass","notes":[[0,36,4,100],[8,43,4,100]]}}. Instruments are beats' names (dj_catalog, dj_set_instrument); omit for the role's default.

set.description: Add it to this set (created if new), in `slot` if given

slot.description: Plan slot index to fill in `set`

steps.description: Loop length in sixteenth steps (default: the longest part)

tools.name: dj_inspired
tools.description: Compose an ORIGINAL piece inspired by an artist or a track and play it: dj_compose with the convention fixed. First read the style in general terms (tempo, key and mode, chord progression type, groove and drum pattern, bass behaviour, sound palette, section form and energy curve) and put that one-line read in `brief`; then write the notes yourself. Never transcribe or closely paraphrase the artist's actual melody, hook, bassline or lyric, and do not take a chord progression note-for-note together with its rhythm; a generic progression and groove in that genre is the point. `inspiredBy` names who or what it is inspired by; it, and the brief, are recorded in the share's note, and the title defaults to "<inspiredBy>-style (original)". Parts, notes, steps and playback are as dj_compose (read its description). Write a full form (16–64 bars, build and drop by leaving parts out of early bars), not one loop.

brief.description: Your one-line style read, e.g. "126 BPM, C# minor, i–VI–III–VII, offbeat bass, syncopated saw stabs, 8-bar build into a drop"

deck.description: A or B (not needed with load false)

energy.description: How hard it hits, 0–1 (kept for set planning)

inspiredBy.description: The artist or track, e.g. "Avicii" or "Avicii – Levels"

key.description: Its key, e.g. "A minor" (kept for set planning)

tuple: Library sounds (vocals, risers, impacts, textures) that come in over the track as parallel tracks on the loop channel: [{loop: name|path, bar: N or [N,…] (the 1-based bar it comes in on), bars?: how long it stays (default one pass of the loop), gain?: dB under unity −24…0 (default −3), keyLock?: keep its pitch at another tempo (default true)}]. Find loops with dj_stock_loops list (category Vocals, Sound Effect, Texture/Atmosphere; near=<the track's bpm>). Launched a bar early so the loop bank's quantizing lands them on the bar; the track is local only, never published.

load.description: false = stage it: save the track (and add it to `set`) without loading a deck, so a whole set can be pre-rolled

tuple: As dj_compose: {role: {instrument?, channel?, every?, from?, until?, notes: [[step, midi, dur?, vel?], …]}} (or a list of segments) with roles kick snare hihat clap bass melody harmony arp.

set.description: Add it to this set (created if new), in `slot` if given

slot.description: Plan slot index to fill in `set`

steps.description: Loop length in sixteenth steps (default: the longest part)

tools.name: dj_import
tools.description: Load a score file from this Mac onto a deck as a raw-nets Petri-net track playing its notes: a Standard MIDI File (.mid / .midi) or MusicXML (.musicxml / .xml / .mxl, partwise; repeats, grace notes and later tempo changes are reported, not played). Quantised to sixteenth steps, the channels sorted into roles (drums by GM note; bass by program or register; chordy channels → harmony; the busiest remaining line → melody), at the file's first tempo. Loads an excerpt of `bars` bars from bar `from` (default 16 from the start, max 64); the reply's `import` says what was kept and dropped (tempo changes, drums with no role, over three notes on one step, notes outside the excerpt) and lists every source channel with its role, so you can re-import with `map` to fix a call. Use `inspect: true` to read that summary without loading. Only for material the user owns or that is public domain / Creative Commons: pass its licence and origin in `source` (kept in the share's note). Does not start playback, and never publishes.

deck.description: A or B (not needed with inspect or load false)

energy.description: How hard it hits, 0–1 (kept for set planning)

inspect.description: Only return the summary; load nothing

key.description: Its key, e.g. "A minor" (kept for set planning)

tuple: Library sounds (vocals, risers, impacts, textures) that come in over the track as parallel tracks on the loop channel: [{loop: name|path, bar: N or [N,…] (the 1-based bar it comes in on), bars?: how long it stays (default one pass of the loop), gain?: dB under unity −24…0 (default −3), keyLock?: keep its pitch at another tempo (default true)}]. Find loops with dj_stock_loops list (category Vocals, Sound Effect, Texture/Atmosphere; near=<the track's bpm>). Launched a bar early so the loop bank's quantizing lands them on the bar; the track is local only, never published.

load.description: false = stage it: save the track (and add it to `set`) without loading a deck, so a whole set can be pre-rolled

tuple: Override roles: {"<track>:<channel>" or "<channel>": role}, role one of bass, melody, harmony, arp, skip (drums are mapped by note)

name.description: Title (default: the file's title or name)

set.description: Add it to this set (created if new), in `slot` if given

slot.description: Plan slot index to fill in `set`

source.description: Origin and licence, e.g. "Mutopia, J.S. Bach, public domain"

tempo.description: BPM override, 40–300 (default: the file's first tempo)

tools.name: dj_compositions
tools.description: The tracks dj_compose, dj_inspired and dj_import have played, kept on disk for reference: each is a JSON file in the compositions folder (reply `directory`; ~/Library/Application Support/dj-vevr-se/compositions/) holding the request that made it (the roll: parts, notes, tempo, brief; for an import its source and report) and the raw-nets envelope. Those three tools save automatically and say where (`saved`). action list (default) returns them newest first with id, name, kind compose|inspired|import, deck, saved, cid, tempo, note and path (optional `query` filters ids, `limit` caps); load {deck, id} puts one back on a deck (id may be any unique part: a title word or the cid tail). Does not start playback. Never publishes.

id.description: The composition's id, or a unique part of it (load)

query.description: Filter the list by part of an id (list)

tools.name: dj_set
tools.description: Plan, pre-roll and play a whole set. A set is a named plan of slots on an energy curve (label, energy 0–1, tempo, key) with a saved composition in each slot, kept in ~/Library/Application Support/dj-vevr-se/sets/. Workflow: `plan` {set, count, shape arc|rise|plateau, bpm [low, high]} (or explicit `slots` [{label, energy, bpm?, key?, bars?}]) → pre-roll tracks with dj_compose / dj_inspired / dj_import using load false, set, slot, energy, key (they are saved and filled into the plan; nothing is loaded) → `sequence` fills the plan from everything saved by energy, tempo (matchable at 1×, ½×, 2×) and key distance on the circle of fifths, and returns `gaps` (slots nothing fits: the brief to compose) and `tempoJumps` → `start` {set, deck?, play?} loads track 1 → `mix` {set, fadeBars?, wait?} hands off to the next track: loads it on the idle deck with its bass EQ down, starts it, tempo-matches and bar-aligns it (the deck's sync), crossfades over fadeBars bars (default the set's, 8) with the bass swapped at the midpoint, stops the old deck. It returns at once (hand-off runs in the app; poll `status`: phase loading|fading|done, progress, warnings such as a tempo gap, bar, barsInTrack); `wait` blocks until done. Other actions: list, show, add {set, id, slot?}, remove {set, index|id}, abort. `auto` {set, on, leadBars?, wander?} makes the app hand off by itself: while the set's deck plays, the next hand-off begins leadBars (default 1) before its fade is due (the track's `mixOutBar`, else fadeBars before its last bar, so the crossfade ends as the track does), and with wander true the walk moves to each incoming deck. `status` shows auto, nextMixAtBar and the bar. Every move is recorded like the performer's own.

action.description: list (default) | show | plan | add | remove | sequence | start | mix | auto | status | abort

tuple: plan with count: [low, high] tempo mapped onto the curve

count.description: plan: generate this many slots on a curve (1–32)

fadeBars.description: Crossfade length in bars, 1–32 (plan: the set's default; mix: this hand-off; add: this track's)

from.description: sequence: all (default, everything saved) | set (only tracks already in it)

id.description: add / remove: a composition id or any unique part of it

keepItems.description: plan: keep the tracks already in the set

leadBars.description: auto: begin the hand-off this many bars before the fade is due (0–8, default 1)

mixOutBar.description: add: bar to start mixing out at (for the auto runner)

on.description: auto: turn the runner on or off

shape.description: plan with count: arc (default) | rise | plateau

wait.description: mix: wait for the hand-off to finish

wander.description: auto: turn Wander on for each incoming deck and off for the outgoing one

tools.name: dj_favorites
tools.description: The starred tracks and samples (also the star by a deck's title and Load ▸ Favorites in the app). action list (default) returns them, newest first, with title, cid, genre, seed (nets) or kind sample + file, and tags; add {deck} stars what a deck plays: its net (instrument changes included) or a sample loaded from a file (Apple Loop or audio file); remove {cid | deck}; load {deck, cid} puts one on a deck (does not start playback); tags {cid | deck, tags} replaces a favorite's tags. Crates (the Load panel's own lists; a crate is a tag, so its loops stay starred): crates lists them (every reply carries crates too); newCrate {crate} makes an empty one; addToCrate {crate, cid | path} puts a favorite, or a stock loop by path (starred as a sample first), in it; removeFromCrate {crate, cid} takes one out (it stays starred); deleteCrate {crate} drops the crate, not its favorites. keepMove {deck, step} toggles the star on the track a move of the deck's walk (dj_state wander.log) led to or played on: the reply's kept says which. A net's cid is its share CID, a sample's "file:" + its path.

action.description: list | add | remove | load | tags | crates | newCrate | addToCrate | removeFromCrate | deleteCrate | keepMove

crate.description: A crate's name (newCrate, addToCrate, removeFromCrate, deleteCrate)

path.description: addToCrate: a stock loop's path, from dj_stock_loops

step.description: keepMove: the move's step, from dj_state wander.log

tags.description: tags: the favorite's tags (they replace the old ones)

tools.name: dj_stock_loops
tools.description: The Apple Loops installed on this Mac (~15k; the Load panel's stock loops). action list (default) filters by `category` (Drums, Bass, Keyboards…; the reply lists them) and `query` words, nearest in tempo to `near` BPM (or the other deck's when `deck` is given) first, up to `limit` (20); load {deck, path} puts one on a deck as a sample with its own tempo as the beat grid (does not start playback); addToRow {path} puts one on the loop row as a clip (dj_state.loops.clips, provenance kind stock), looping under the mixer from the next launch boundary in time with the decks; the same loop twice is one clip. A set with a stock loop on the row is never published.

near.description: Sort by closeness to this BPM

query.description: Words to match in name, pack, genre, subcategory

tools.name: dj_copy_deck
tools.description: Load the net track on one deck onto the other, instrument changes included, from its start (at the next bar if that deck is playing). Returns the target deck.

tools.name: dj_set_instrument
tools.description: Change the beats instrument a role plays on a net deck (dj_state's `instruments`): it picks the synth voice and, through its category, the sampled sound. Stored as the share's `tracks` override, so it records, stars and shares. The track reloads from its start (at the next bar if playing): use it on the deck that isn't live. Roles sharing a channel (the drum kit) change together. A wrong instrument lists the choices.

instrument.description: e.g. reese, supersaw (an error lists the choices)

tools.name: dj_variations
tools.description: Saved variations: named ways to play an instrument (the sound panel's chips), kept across launches by instrument name. action list (default) {instrument?}: each instrument's variations (name, params — the voiceTweak values — and useSynth); save {deck, channel, name}: keep what that net deck's channel sounds like now (its voiceTweak / voiceSynth; the same name replaces it); apply {deck, channel, name, instrument?}: play one on the channel, as voiceTweak / voiceSynth acts — an instrument other than the channel's reloads the track with it first (as dj_set_instrument); rename {instrument | deck + channel, name, to}; delete {instrument | deck + channel, name}. dj_state's voices show each channel's instrument, `variation` (the one it matches) and `variations`. Errors list the channels and variations there are.

instrument.description: list: only this one; apply: play it with this instrument (default: the channel's); rename / delete: whose variation

tools.name: dj_minecraft_events
tools.description: Minecraft gameplay fires stingers. Pass what the minecraft server's mc_recent_events returned (its array of {at, source, event, params}, oldest first) as `events`; each event is mapped through voices/minecraft-events.json (log:death → stinger 0, log:advancement → 1, minecraft:notification/players/joined → 2) and played on `deck` (default: the focus deck), recorded like a button. The app keeps a cursor, so re-sending an overlapping window fires each event once; a deck takes at most one stinger a bar (the rest are skipped, with the reason). prime: take the events without playing them (start a polling loop without replaying the backlog). Stingers need a net deck.

deck.description: A or B (default: the focus deck)

prime.description: Take the events without playing any

tools.name: dj_press_pad
tools.description: Press a pad on the APC mini grid (the real one, or the on-screen one, which this shows). Recorded as MIDI, exactly like the hardware.

group.description: pads (8×8 grid, 0-63) | track (0-7) | scene (0-7) | drumPads (0-15); dj_catalog lists what each is bound to

shift.description: true to hold SHIFT around the press. SHIFT + pads is the loop page: loops 1-64 read like text, top-left (pad 56) = loop 1, top row 1-8, the next row down 9-16 (in/out on the downbeat)

tools.name: dj_audition
tools.description: Play one instrument on the Mac's output, outside the decks: a strummed chord and a few notes, or the MIDI notes you give. Also saved as a WAV; returns its path, level and which sound it uses (pluck, or the wavetable family it folds into).

instrument.description: An instrument name from dj_catalog, e.g. acoustic-guitar

tuple: Optional MIDI notes, played 0.3 s apart (e.g. [40, 45, 50, 55])

play.description: false to only render the WAV (default true)

tools.name: dj_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the live DJApp window (decks, net rings, timeline, pads) and return it as a PNG image. Also saved to disk; the path is in the text part.

path.description: Where to save the PNG (default: ~/Library/Application Support/DJApp/shots/)

tools.name: dj_view
tools.description: Show or hide the main window's panels: the Soundboard (every loop as a big pad), Controllers, Map, Scopes, the on-screen APC pads and the Loops master FX strip; fold each deck's sections open or shut; set what the scope panel shows; open, close or set the Stage window. Leave anything out to keep it as it is; returns what shows now.

controllers.description: Every controller drawn with its bindings

loopMasterFx.description: The Loops row's master FX strip

soundboard.description: The Soundboard: one pad per loop, scenes on top

tools.name: dj_settings
tools.description: The monitoring settings: pfl {A, B} (a deck's headphone cue), headphoneMix (0 cue only … 1 master only in the headphones), headphoneLevel (0…1), awake (keep the screen from sleeping) and inpulseOutput (master → the Inpulse's outputs 1/2, cue → 3/4; restarts the audio engine, an error when no Inpulse is connected). Only the keys given change (a bad one changes nothing); returns headphones {mix, level, pfl}, awake and inpulseOutput as they stand (dj_state shows the same). These are monitoring, not performance: they never reach the master mix, so a recorded session does not record them.

awake.description: Keep the display awake while the app is open

inpulseOutput.description: Route master and cue to the Inpulse's audio outputs

pfl.description: Deck name → cue on/off, e.g. {"A": true, "B": false}

tools.name: dj_record
tools.description: Start (on: true) or stop (on: false) recording a session. Stopping saves it locally and returns its CID. Publishing stays a button in the app: it is public.

on.description: true to start, false to stop and save

tools.name: dj_notes
tools.description: Notes on tracks. A note is text on what a deck plays — a net track by its share CID (the same genre, seed and settings is the same track, so its notes come back whenever it plays again), a sample by its content id, a loop clip by id — at the bar it was on. action list (default): every note, or {deck} the notes on what that deck plays now, or {target} those on a target key ("track:<cid>", "sample:<id>", "clip:<id>"); add {deck, text}: a note at the deck's current bar, or {clip, text} on a loop clip; edit {id, text}; delete {id}. Notes are journal events (dj_journal), so the History panel and `djctl journal show` list them.

tools.name: dj_loops
tools.description: The Loops row's buttons that are not deck actions. action list (default) returns dj_state.loops; undo puts back the loop last taken off the row (the row's Undo, for a few seconds after dj_perform clipRemove; clipRestore {id} brings back any removed loop); loadSource {id, deck} loads the track a clip was taken from onto deck A or B (a net composed again, at the section it was in; a sample while its audio is in memory; does not start playback); export {id, path} writes a clip's audio as a 32-bit float stereo WAV to path (an absolute .wav path, or a folder: named after the clip) and returns its frames and sampleRate; stopAll takes every looping clip out on the next launch boundary (a clipLoop off each, recorded) and returns the ids stopped. Starting, stopping, gain, crop, mute, solo and a clip's FX (clipFx) are dj_perform ops.

path.description: export: an absolute .wav path, or a folder

tools.name: dj_journal
tools.description: The app's journal: the always-on log of every state change this run (deck actions, controller MIDI, favorites, crates, variations, locks, notes), the record a run is rebuilt from (`djctl journal replay`). action list (default): the file and its latest entries (seq, time, engine frame, kind, a summary, and the event as JSON), newest last. action rewind {seq}: put the app back where it stood at that seq — the journal is replayed to it, the decks, loop row, mixer and stores reset to the result — and journal a `rewind <seq>` mark and a checkpoint (nothing is deleted: the journal is append-only). Returns the checkpoint written and any clips or samples whose audio was gone.

kind.description: Only entries of this kind, e.g. act, midi, note.add (prefix: note.)

seq.description: rewind: the entry to go back to (its seq, from list)
